title: Infectious episodes before and after a marathon race
authors: Ekblom B, Ekblom O, Malm C
journal: Scandinavian Journal of Medicine & Science in Sports
population: 1694 Stockholm Marathon 2000 runners (17% of all finishers); two questionnaires on self-reported infectious episodes in the 3 weeks before and the 3 weeks after the race
findings: Infection incidence was 17% in the 3 weeks before and 19% in the 3 weeks after the race, with no significant difference between women and men.
Among runners without a pre-race infection the post-race incidence was 16%; among runners with a pre-race infection 33% had a post-race infection (P < 0.05 versus pre-IE incidence).

Logistic regression: younger age, pre-race health status and, for men only, nausea during and after the race explained post-race infections; no relation to training volume 6 months before, finishing time or socioeconomic and demographic factors.
Authors conclude the study does not support the open window theory in recreational runners, and suggest increased infection rates can be caused by strenuous exercise too soon after an infection.
limitations: Self-reported infections by questionnaire (recall bias); the abstract does not state when each questionnaire was completed, so the cohort label is approximate; marathon only, recreational runners; not ultra distance; no immune-function markers.
implications: There is no evidence here that a 3-week post-marathon immune window justifies a longer hold; do not lengthen the hold on immunological grounds for marathons.
A runner who was ill before the race is the high-risk group (33% vs 16%): recent illness is a reasonable reason to delay the return ramp, and check-ins should ask about illness and not only soreness.
Post-race nausea in men tracked later infection but is too weak and too narrow to be a gate.

verification.notes: Crossref (online 2005-10-27; authors Ekblom, Ekblom, Malm) and abstract re-read (PMID 16895535); all numbers match. Flagged the unverifiable design timing. The study does not cover ultras, so relevance to the ultra holds is indirect.
